qc.label_under_test: the hyphenated '-so' in the ironic hedge 'not-so-X' ('a not-so-quiet evening'), as against unhyphenated 'not so', 'so-so' and other uses of so

neighbours.label: a degree/hedge word or hyphen inside a compound modifier placed directly before its noun, strongest at the '-so' of 'a not-so-quiet evening' ('a medically necessary procedure', 'a highly-anticipated season'); quiet when the same words come after 'was'
fire: We spent a not-so-quiet evening listening to the neighbors' band rehearse.
The surgeon explained that it was a medically necessary procedure, not a cosmetic one.
Fans finally got to watch the highly-anticipated season premiere last night.
She gave a not-so-subtle hint that she wanted the last slice of cake.
It was a deeply moving speech that left the audience in tears.
The startup hired a well-known designer to rebrand its app.
They moved into a fairly small apartment near the train station.
He wrote a surprisingly thoughtful review of the old film.
quiet: The evening was not so quiet once the neighbors' band started rehearsing.
The surgeon explained that the procedure was medically necessary, not cosmetic.
The season premiere that fans watched last night was highly anticipated.
Her hint that she wanted the last slice of cake was not so subtle.
The speech was deeply moving and left the audience in tears.
The startup hired a designer who was well known to rebrand its app.
The apartment they moved into near the train station was fairly small.
His review of the old film was surprisingly thoughtful.

predictions: Not-so and medically necessary / highly-anticipated should fire; plain adverb+adjective items (well-known, fairly small, deeply moving) probably weak, so median fire may miss 0.20 or AUROC may fall under 0.90.
